questions.question: What is the standard sea level atmospheric pressure?
questions.explanation: Standard sea level pressure is 29.92 inches of mercury (Hg), which is equivalent to 1013.25 millibars (mb) or 14.7 psi.
steps: Recognize the question is about standard atmosphere.
Recall the standard value: 29.92 inches Hg.
Eliminate distractors with incorrect units or values.

questions.question: What is V1 speed?
questions.explanation: V1 is the critical engine failure recognition speed during takeoff. Beyond V1, the takeoff must continue even if an emergency occurs.
steps: Identify V1 as a takeoff speed.

questions.question: What is the purpose of trim tabs?
questions.explanation: Trim tabs help pilots maintain a desired flight attitude by reducing the control force needed on the yoke or stick.
steps: Identify trim tabs as small surfaces on control surfaces.
Recall their function: reduce pilot workload.
questions.fastStrategy: Trim tabs = less effort to hold attitude.
